title: Exhaust suddenly loud
h1: Why is my exhaust suddenly so loud?
metaDesc: Exhaust suddenly loud or roaring? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's a leak, a broken pipe or a stolen converter, how urgent it is, and what to do next.
synonyms: car sounds like a race car
loud car when I press the gas
intro: When a car suddenly gets loud, exhaust gas is usually escaping before it reaches the muffler. Often that's a rusted or broken part, but it can also mean exhaust fumes are getting into the cabin, which is dangerous. These questions help you tell the difference and decide what to do.
safety: If you smell exhaust inside the car or feel headachy, dizzy or drowsy, stop driving, get out and get fresh air.
If part of the exhaust is dragging on the ground, pull over. It can come loose or start a fire in dry grass.
Never idle the car in a closed garage, and don't sit in a parked, running car with an exhaust leak.
Don't touch the exhaust after driving. It stays hot enough to burn for a long time.

q_danger.q: Do you notice either of these?
q_danger.help: Exhaust fumes contain carbon monoxide, which you can't see or smell. A fume smell inside the car means it may be getting in too.

opts.a: An exhaust smell inside the car, or headache, dizziness or drowsiness while driving
Something hanging down or scraping the road under the car
Suddenly and very loud the first time I started the car after it was parked
Suddenly, right after hitting a pothole, curb, speed bump or something in the road
It has been getting louder gradually

q_where.q: Where does the noise seem to come from, and what does it sound like?
q_where.help: Listen from outside the car while someone else starts it and gently revs it in Park.

opts.a: Near the engine: a ticking or puffing sound, loudest on a cold start
Under the middle of the car: a deep roar or rumble when accelerating
From the back, near the muffler or tailpipe

result.title: Exhaust fumes may be getting into the cabin
result.now: Pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone out into fresh air. Don't drive it again until the leak is fixed. Have it towed.
if: If anyone has a headache, nausea, confusion or drowsiness that doesn't clear quickly in fresh air, call 911 or get medical help right away.
If the smell only appears with the windows down at low speed and nobody feels unwell, it still needs to be fixed before the car is driven again.
If anyone feels unwell again once back in the car, even after airing it out, don't use it until the exhaust has been repaired.
result.why: Exhaust contains carbon monoxide, a gas you can't see that can make you sick or cause you to pass out without warning. A loud exhaust means there's a leak, and a fume smell inside means the gas may be reaching you.

causes.name: Exhaust leak under the cabin
causes.clues: The noise is loudest under the middle of the car, and the smell is worse when stopped.

causes.name: Leak near the engine reaching the vents
causes.clues: The smell comes through the vents, especially with the fan on.

causes.name: Rusted pipe with holes in several places
causes.clues: An older car with heavy rust underneath.

result.title: Part of the exhaust has broken loose
result.now: Pull over somewhere safe and away from dry grass. Don't drive it with the pipe dragging. Call roadside assistance or a tow.
if: If you see smoke or flames under the car, get everyone away and call 911.
A roadside technician may be able to secure the pipe temporarily once it's cool, but it still needs a proper repair soon.
If you smell fuel or see fluid dripping near the damaged pipe, keep everyone away from the car and call for help. Fuel and brake lines run close to the exhaust.
result.why: Exhaust pipes hang from rubber hangers and metal brackets. When one breaks or a rusted pipe snaps, the pipe can drag, catch on the road, damage other parts or come loose in traffic. The hot metal can also set dry grass or debris on fire.

causes.name: Broken rubber hanger or bracket
causes.clues: The pipe hangs low but is still in one piece.

causes.name: Rusted pipe that snapped
causes.clues: An older car, and the noise got very loud at the same time.

causes.name: Impact damage
causes.clues: It started after hitting something on the road.

you: From a safe spot, look under the car to see what's hanging. Don't touch the exhaust until it has cooled.

result.title: The catalytic converter may have been stolen
result.now: With the car parked and cool, look under the car, between the engine and the muffler, for a missing section or pipes with clean, freshly cut ends. If it's gone, report it to the police and your insurer, and arrange the repair within the next few days. Until then, use the car as little as possible and never sit in it while it idles.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car, or anyone gets a headache, dizziness or drowsiness, don't drive it. Have it towed.
If nothing is missing, the noise is likely a broken pipe or gasket. Have the exhaust inspected within a few days.
If a cut pipe end is hanging low or scraping, or you see damaged wires or fluid dripping near the cut, don't drive it. Thieves sometimes nick nearby lines.
result.why: A car that's suddenly very loud the first time you start it after it was parked, with no warning before, is a common sign of catalytic converter theft. Thieves cut it out in minutes. Without it, the car is loud, the check engine light will usually come on, and exhaust exits under the middle of the car.

causes.name: Stolen catalytic converter
causes.clues: Freshly cut pipe ends, and the car was parked overnight or in a public lot.
causes.against: If all the exhaust parts are still there, theft is ruled out.

causes.name: Broken or separated exhaust pipe
causes.clues: A rusted joint or a pipe that's come apart, with no cut marks.

causes.name: Blown exhaust gasket
causes.clues: Loud, but not as loud, and there's no visible damage.

you: With the car parked and cool, look underneath for a missing section or cut pipe ends.
Take photos for the police and insurance report.

result.title: The impact may have broken or knocked loose part of the exhaust
result.now: Once the car is cool, look underneath for a bent, cracked or separated pipe. Get it inspected within the next few days, and keep any driving short.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car, don't drive it. Have it towed.
If something is hanging or scraping, pull over and call for a tow.
If you also see fluid dripping, the impact may have damaged other parts. Have it checked before driving.
If a warning light comes on, the brake pedal feels different, or you smell fuel after the hit, don't drive it until it's been checked. Something besides the exhaust may be damaged.
result.why: Exhaust pipes run low under the car, so they're often the first thing to hit a curb or road debris. A hit can crack a pipe, break a joint or tear a hanger, which lets exhaust escape before the muffler.

causes.name: Cracked or separated pipe joint
causes.clues: A visible gap or a pipe that's out of line.

causes.name: Damaged flex pipe
causes.clues: A woven, braided section of pipe that's torn or crushed.

causes.name: Crushed or punctured muffler
causes.clues: A dent or hole in the muffler, with the noise loudest at the back.

you: With the car cool, look underneath for dents, gaps or hanging parts.
Look for any fluid drips on the ground under the car.

result.title: Possibly a leak at the exhaust manifold near the engine
result.now: Book an exhaust inspection when convenient, and mention that the ticking is loudest on a cold start.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car, especially through the vents, stop driving it and have it checked right away.
If you smell burning plastic or rubber under the hood, have it checked soon. Hot exhaust may be reaching nearby wiring or hoses.
If the check engine light flashes or the engine runs rough, have it checked within a day or two. A leak near the engine can upset the sensors that control fuel.
result.why: The exhaust manifold collects gas right where it leaves the engine. A cracked manifold or a blown gasket leaks in quick puffs, which sounds like ticking. It's often loudest when cold because the metal shrinks and the gap is bigger until it warms up.

causes.name: Blown exhaust manifold gasket
causes.clues: Ticking that matches engine speed and quiets down as the engine warms.

causes.name: Cracked exhaust manifold
causes.clues: Common on some trucks and older engines, with sooty marks near the crack.

causes.name: Broken or missing manifold bolt
causes.clues: Black soot at one corner of the manifold.

you: Listen near the engine on a cold start, staying clear of belts and the fan.
Look for black soot marks where the exhaust meets the engine.

result.title: Possibly a leak in the pipe or a joint under the middle of the car
result.now: Have the exhaust inspected within the next few days. Until then, don't sit in the car with the engine idling for long periods.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car or feel headachy or drowsy, stop driving and get fresh air. Have it towed.
If the check engine light comes on, mention it. A leak near an oxygen sensor can affect how the engine runs.
If you see smoke or smell burning from under the car, pull over and turn the engine off. A loose pipe can heat up nearby parts or debris.
result.why: The middle section of the exhaust runs right under where you sit. A leak there makes a deep roar under acceleration and is the most likely place for fumes to reach the cabin, which is why it shouldn't wait.

causes.name: Worn or torn flex pipe
causes.clues: A woven, braided section of pipe near the front that's frayed or cracked. Common on front-wheel-drive cars.

causes.name: Rusted pipe or failed joint gasket
causes.clues: Heavy rust or black soot at a joint.

causes.name: Damaged catalytic converter shell or connection
causes.clues: The noise is near the converter, sometimes with a rattle.

you: With the car cool, look under the middle of the car for rust holes, gaps or black soot marks.

result.title: Often a rusted or damaged muffler or tailpipe
result.now: Book an exhaust inspection when convenient. Avoid idling with the trunk or rear hatch open.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car, especially in the back seat or with the hatch closed, stop driving it and have it checked before using the car again.
If the noise gets much louder suddenly, or something starts rattling or hanging, get it checked within a few days.
result.why: The muffler and tailpipe sit at the back, where water and road salt collect, so they often rust from the inside out. A hole there makes the car louder and is farther from the cabin, but fumes can still get in through worn trunk or hatch seals, especially when you're stopped.

causes.name: Rusted-through muffler
causes.clues: An older car, rust spots or holes, often on the bottom or seams.

causes.name: Rusted tailpipe or joint at the muffler
causes.clues: Soot or a gap where the pipe enters the muffler.

causes.name: Broken baffles inside the muffler
causes.clues: A rattle when you tap the muffler (when it's cold).

you: With the car cool, look at the muffler and tailpipe for rust holes or soot.
With the engine idling and the car in Park, carefully listen from behind for where the noise is loudest.

result.title: There's likely an exhaust leak somewhere. Have it inspected
result.now: Book an exhaust inspection, ideally within the next week or two. Keep idling to a minimum until then.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car or feel headachy or drowsy, stop driving and get fresh air.
If something starts dragging or the noise gets much louder suddenly, pull over and call for help.
If you see smoke or smell burning from under the car, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: A suddenly loud exhaust usually means gas is escaping somewhere before it should. With the car on a lift, a technician can usually find the spot quickly.

causes.name: Rusted muffler or pipe
causes.clues: An older car, or one driven where roads are salted.

causes.name: Failed gasket or flex pipe
causes.clues: A rumble or puffing under the front or middle of the car.

causes.name: Broken hanger letting a joint separate
causes.clues: Rattling or clunking along with the noise.

you: Record a short video with sound of the car starting and revving in Park.
Look under the car for anything hanging low.
